in: Case data model: two record types (Support, Billing) with their Support Processes, the Email-Support / Email-Billing / Web Origin values, and the Account fields the routing and SLA layers read (Region__c, Support_Tier__c) [Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q19, Q85]
Page layouts per Case record type plus a Case compact layout, with 'Assign using active assignment rule' defaulted on for manual entry [Q3, Q24, Q83]

Access model: a minimal base profile per team over permission set groups for Tier 1, Tier 2 and Billing, covering Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement and the Service app [Q3, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q86, Q87]
An intake-bypass Custom Permission on an integration permission set, so API-created cases are never blocked by a rule aimed at agents [Q56]
Three Case queues (Tier 1 General, Tier 2 Engineering, Billing) with role-and-public-group membership and no named users [Q26, Q29, Q30, Q88, Q89]
Case org-wide default Private plus a criteria-based sharing rule opening Support cases to Tier 2; nothing opens Billing cases to Tier 1 [Q13 (deferred, conservative reading), Q80]
Case validation rules with the intake bypass, component-field formulas and final message text written at design time [Q5, Q56, Q58, Q59, Q93]

Email-to-Case for support@acme.example and billing@acme.example with per-address Origin stamping, bounce-on-unauthorised-sender, requeue-on-over-limit and saveEmailHeaders on [Q15, Q17, Q18, Q19, Q21, Q23, Q74]
Web-to-Case intake for the website form at ~60 submissions a day [Q15, Q66]
Case assignment rules routing on Origin and account support tier with a Tier 1 General catch-all, plus auto-response rules [Q24, Q25, Q26, Q27]

Classic acknowledgement and escalation email templates sent from support@ and billing@ as verified org-wide addresses, carrying the case number and the thread token [Q22, Q28, Q60, Q61, Q62, Q63, Q64, Q78]
Queue-based Omni-Channel push for Tier 1 granted by profile; Tier 2 and Billing pull from queue list views [Q31, Q36, Q37]

Business Hours for EMEA (London 08:00-18:00), the US (New York 08:00-20:00, org default) and a 24/7 Severity 1 calendar, plus regional holidays and a named yearly maintenance owner [Q38, Q39, Q40, Q90]
Entitlement process and First Response milestone types for Premier (4 business hours) and Standard (1 business day), with the Case's calendar as the explicit authority [Q38, Q50, Q51, Q53]
A before-save record-triggered Flow stamping EntitlementId, BusinessHoursId and the Priority default, with a documented no-matching-account fallback [Q16, Q40, Q48]
Case escalation rules: an 8-business-hour Tier 2 entry on the Case calendar (480 minutes, from CaseCreation) and a 24/7 Severity 1 entry, both deployed inactive [Q42, Q43, Q44, Q45, Q46, Q47, Q91]
Pull list views for Tier 2 and Billing plus a saved report on escalated, still-open Cases in a shared folder [Q31, Q91]

A sandbox proof: Partial Copy object selection (Account, Contact, Case, Entitlement, EmailMessage), post-refresh re-pointing of the routing addresses and the form endpoint, and UAT test cases covering all three intake channels and the deny cases, run by a named tester per team [Q68, Q72, Q74, Q76, Q77, Q78, Q80, Q83, Q84, Q94, Q96, Q97]

Documentation: the ten-section configuration workbook, an INVEST story backlog, the traceability matrix, package.xml and a deploy-order note ending in a validate-only command [Q94, workbook and RTM skills]
out: Phone / telephony, chat, knowledge base and customer portal — named out of scope by the requirement itself and reinforced by Q30 (Case is the only queue-supported object) and Q12 (employees only)
Skills-based Omni-Channel routing — descoped by Q37: the requirement describes three team queues and no skill dimension
Person Accounts — descoped by Q6: Acme is B2B, so Cases hang off Business Accounts and Contacts
Lead routing, Lead queues and lead-convert ownership — descoped by Q30: no Lead work item is described
Migration of historical cases from the shared mailbox — descoped by Q4 and Q58: no Salesforce Case records exist and none are being loaded

Field-level masking of billing data on a shared Case record — blocked on deferred Q13; the plan takes the record-level reading instead (assumption A1) and this alternative shape is out until Q13 is answered
An elapsed-working-time field for reports or code — blocked on deferred Q41 (assumption A8)
Milestone clock stop / pause (isStopped) and who may stop it — blocked on deferred Q52 (assumption A10)
Entitlement versioning and its owner — blocked on deferred Q92 (assumption A24)
A milestone end-condition other than case closure — blocked on deferred Q49 (assumption A9)

The sandbox ladder itself: allocation, refresh floors, which environments hold copied production records, and post-copy automation — blocked on deferred Q69, Q70, Q71, Q73 and Q75 (assumptions A17-A21). Only the single proof sandbox from Q68 and Q72 is planned
Test-data creation mechanism (UI vs Data Loader vs Bulk API vs REST) — blocked on deferred Q79 (assumption A22)
The reporting backlog beyond the escalation monitoring report — blocked on deferred Q65 (assumption A14)
An as-is process map of what the support team does today — blocked on deferred Q67 (assumption A16)
Per-expected-result evidence design and the deny-case pre-condition audit — blocked on deferred Q81 and Q82 (assumptions A23 and A15); the UAT pack carries placeholders a human closes

A defined rule for what must NOT happen automatically, and who repairs a wrong automation — blocked on deferred Q14 (assumption A2). Until it is answered the stamping flow writes only into null fields
Deployment to any org — out of scope for this layer by contract: the plan produces deploy-ready artefacts, a deploy order and a validate-only command, and a human deploys

fit_gap.requirement: Two Case processes (support and finance) with different status and reason values
fit_gap.note: Record types plus Support Processes are point-and-click configuration on Case; admin/record-types-and-page-layouts carries the picklist-per-record-type mechanics.

fit_gap.requirement: Three teams with different object, field and app access, membership changing monthly
fit_gap.note: Permission set groups over a minimal base profile; admin/permission-set-architecture and admin/permission-set-group-composition give the composition and muting rules.

fit_gap.requirement: Work pools per team whose membership list changes monthly without a deploy
fit_gap.note: Queues whose members are public groups and roles, per admin/queues-and-public-groups; usernames never enter the metadata (Q29).

fit_gap.requirement: Finance queries worked only by Finance
fit_gap.note: Case OWD Private plus a criteria-based sharing rule is standard sharing (sharing-selection Q3), but the requirement never says whether the restriction is record-level or field-level — Q13 is deferred, so half of this is unresolved and the conservative reading is planned.

fit_gap.requirement: Cases arrive by email to two addresses at ~400 a day
fit_gap.note: Email-to-Case routing addresses with per-address Origin, bounce and requeue behaviour and saveEmailHeaders, per admin/email-to-case-configuration.

fit_gap.requirement: Cases arrive from a website form at ~60 a day
fit_gap.note: Native Web-to-Case covers the band (integration-pattern-selection Q5 rules out Bulk and iPaaS by volume), but Q66's answer itself says to confirm whether the form posts directly or through middleware — so the intake contract is provisional.

fit_gap.requirement: An owner within the first minute of case creation
fit_gap.note: Case assignment rules fire synchronously at create on all three channels; admin/assignment-rules references/routing-selector.md row 1 is the mechanism, and decision D3 records that no tree covers it.

fit_gap.requirement: An acknowledgement carrying the case number within the first minute
fit_gap.note: Case auto-response rules with a Classic template that merges CaseNumber and keeps the thread token, per admin/email-templates-and-alerts (Q61, Q62, Q64).

fit_gap.requirement: Priority set from what the form or email tells us, within the first minute
fit_gap.note: Web-to-Case can map a form field straight to Priority, but email carries no structured priority, so the before-save flow can only apply a default into a null field. Q16 asks for priority 'from what the form or email tells us' and no answer says how an email conveys it — the email half of this requirement is not closed by any step.

fit_gap.requirement: Pushed work for Tier 1 when agents are available; pull for Tier 2 and Billing
fit_gap.note: Omni-Channel queue-based routing granted by profile is standard Service Cloud configuration, but four of the questions that shape a routing configuration (Q32-Q35) were deferred, so the capacity model is provisional. Decision D4 records that no tree covers the choice.

fit_gap.requirement: The SLA clock running on the right regional calendar within the first minute
fit_gap.note: Business Hours per region plus a before-save flow that resolves Account.Region__c to a calendar with the US as default (Q40); admin/business-hours-and-holidays carries the default-calendar and holiday rules.

fit_gap.requirement: First response within 4 business hours (Premier) or 1 business day (Standard), pausing on weekends and regional holidays
fit_gap.note: Entitlement process plus First Response milestone types with the Case's calendar as the explicit authority (Q51); admin/entitlements-and-milestones covers the two-milestone-type question Q53 raises.

fit_gap.requirement: Severity 1 outages tracked 24/7 with a clock that never pauses
fit_gap.note: A 24/7 BusinessHours record plus an escalation entry with businessHoursSource = None (Q43); admin/escalation-rules documents the None-source behaviour.

fit_gap.requirement: Anything untouched for 8 business hours escalates to Tier 2
fit_gap.note: Case escalation rule, 480 minutes from CaseCreation, businessHoursSource = Case, action = reassign to the Tier 2 queue plus notify (Q42, Q45, Q46). Decision D7 records that no tree covers the engine choice.

fit_gap.requirement: Replies to customers go from support@ for general cases and billing@ for finance cases
fit_gap.note: Verified org-wide email addresses restricted to the profiles that need them (Q60), with the acknowledgement itself sent from support@ on both channels per Q22 and Q28.

fit_gap.requirement: Prove it works in a sandbox before customers see it
fit_gap.note: A Partial Copy proof sandbox with the five objects Q72 names, the post-refresh re-pointing Q74 demands and per-channel UAT cases Q84 requires is buildable. It is partial because Q69-Q71, Q73, Q75 and Q79 are deferred, so the environment ladder and the test-data mechanism behind the proof are undefined.

fit_gap.requirement: A deployable, reviewable record of the whole configuration
fit_gap.note: The ten-section configuration workbook plus an RTM and package.xml; admin/configuration-workbook-authoring fixes the sections and the one-agent-per-row rule.

assumptions.text: Billing-case confidentiality is a record-level restriction: a Tier 1 agent cannot open a Billing case at all, rather than opening it with a field hidden.
assumptions.because: Q13 was deferred; the conservative option is the more restrictive one, because a wrongly-open record cannot be un-seen while a wrongly-hidden field is a one-line fix. (source: deferred clarification Q13)

assumptions.text: No automation overwrites a value a human has already set: the stamping flow writes only into null fields, and the support manager repairs a wrong automation result by hand.
assumptions.because: Q14 was deferred; writing only into nulls is the option that cannot destroy an agent's work. (source: deferred clarification Q14)

assumptions.text: The org is on Lightning Threading (Email-to-Case thread identifier in the headers), and every customer-facing template still carries the visible thread token as a belt-and-braces fallback.
assumptions.because: Q20 was deferred; Q64's answer already requires the token, so keeping it costs nothing and covers the legacy-threading case too. (source: deferred clarification Q20)

assumptions.text: Omni-Channel pushes Case only, and agent capacity is released when the case is closed rather than when the tab is closed.
assumptions.because: Q32 was deferred; release-on-close is the conservative choice because it cannot hand an agent a second case while the first is still open. (source: deferred clarification Q32)

assumptions.text: A Tier 1 agent's capacity is 5 units and a Case is worth 1 unit, recorded in provisional-capacity-assumptions.md as provisional.
assumptions.because: Q33 was deferred and no skill supplies a defensible default; the numbers exist only so the artefact is well-formed and are marked provisional in the artefact itself. (source: deferred clarification Q33)

assumptions.text: Routing model is Least Active, with the longest-idle agent as the tie-breaker.
assumptions.because: Q34 was deferred; Least Active is the conservative choice because it does not concentrate work on whoever happens to be logged in longest. (source: deferred clarification Q34)

assumptions.text: A pushed case that nobody accepts within the push timeout returns to the Tier 1 General queue rather than being pushed to the next agent.
assumptions.because: Q35 was deferred; returning to the queue is the option that cannot silently lose a case. (source: deferred clarification Q35)

assumptions.text: No report or code needs elapsed working time, so no working-time field is built in this phase.
assumptions.because: Q41 was deferred; building a field nobody asked for is the more expensive error here, and adding one later is additive. (source: deferred clarification Q41)

assumptions.text: The first-response commitment ends when the milestone is completed, and the entitlement process ends when the case is closed.
assumptions.because: Q49 was deferred; case closure is the platform default and the only end condition the requirement names. (source: deferred clarification Q49)

assumptions.text: The SLA clock is never stopped in this phase; no stop reason and no stop permission is configured.
assumptions.because: Q52 was deferred; a clock that cannot be stopped cannot be stopped wrongly, and adding stop reasons later is additive. (source: deferred clarification Q52)

assumptions.text: Every validation rule fires on a field the user edits on the Case itself; no rule reaches into a child record.
assumptions.because: Q54 was deferred; a rule scoped to the Case is the one that cannot fire on a save the user did not make. (source: deferred clarification Q54)

assumptions.text: No automation writes the fields the validation rules guard after save; the before-save stamping flow is the only writer and it runs before validation.
assumptions.because: Q55 was deferred; this is consistent with D1 and with Q27's single-owner-writer answer, and it is the assumption the artefacts must be checked against. (source: deferred clarification Q55)

assumptions.text: Every field a validation rule attaches its error to is present on both Case layouts.
assumptions.because: Q57 was deferred; the alternative produces an error the user cannot see, so the plan assumes the layouts carry the field and M1-S02's checker is what proves it. (source: deferred clarification Q57)

assumptions.text: The only reporting requirement in this phase is the escalation monitoring report Q91 names.
assumptions.because: Q65 was deferred; building one named report is smaller than guessing a reporting backlog. (source: deferred clarification Q65)

assumptions.text: For every deny case, the persona is set up without the granting permission set and nothing else is already blocking the path.
assumptions.because: Q82 was deferred; assuming a second blocker would let a test pass for the wrong reason, so the plan assumes the single-cause case and makes the tester record what they saw. (source: deferred clarification Q82)

assumptions.text: The as-is process is the shared mailbox described in the requirement and nothing more; no as-is map is produced.
assumptions.because: Q67 was deferred; the requirement's own first line is the only as-is evidence available. (source: deferred clarification Q67)

assumptions.text: One sandbox is available for the proof and its refresh is not contended.
assumptions.because: Q69 was deferred; the plan needs exactly one environment and assumes no more than that. (source: deferred clarification Q69)

assumptions.text: The proof sandbox holds copied production Account and Contact records and is readable only by the named testers and the admin lead.
assumptions.because: Q70 was deferred; Q72 already requires Account and Contact to be seeded, so the restrictive readership is the conservative pairing. (source: deferred clarification Q70)

assumptions.text: No environment in the ladder has a refresh floor that blocks the proof window.
assumptions.because: Q71 was deferred; the plan does not schedule a refresh, so the assumption is only that none is forced on it. (source: deferred clarification Q71)

assumptions.text: Post-copy automation does exactly what Q74 requires: re-point the Email-to-Case routing addresses and the website form endpoint, and nothing else.
assumptions.because: Q73 was deferred; the narrowest post-copy job is the one least likely to touch production-shaped data. (source: deferred clarification Q73)

assumptions.text: UAT runs in the same proof sandbox, and no refresh is booked inside the UAT window.
assumptions.because: Q75 was deferred; a refresh mid-UAT would invalidate the run, so the plan assumes it does not happen and the sandbox proof plan records it as a precondition. (source: deferred clarification Q75)

assumptions.text: Test data is created through the UI by the named testers, not by a bulk load.
assumptions.because: Q79 was deferred; UI creation is the path the personas actually use (Q84) and needs no additional tooling decision. (source: deferred clarification Q79)

assumptions.text: Each expected result is evidenced by a screen the tester can point at, plus the case record itself; no query or file evidence is designed in this phase.
assumptions.because: Q81 was deferred; screen-plus-record is the evidence a non-technical tester can actually produce. (source: deferred clarification Q81)

assumptions.text: Entitlement versioning is off and no next version is owned.
assumptions.because: Q92 was deferred; versioning off is the platform default and the state the first release should ship in. (source: deferred clarification Q92)

assumptions.text: The validation deploy runs before sign-off, and the QA or BA lead named in Q97 accepts any deferred defect.
assumptions.because: Q95 was deferred; running validation before sign-off is the ordering that cannot sign off an unvalidated build. (source: deferred clarification Q95)

decisions.decision: Stamp Case.EntitlementId, Case.BusinessHoursId and the Priority default in one before-save record-triggered Flow rather than in Apex or an after-save Flow.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q2. Does the logic run in under ~10s and touch only fields on the record itself?
    ├── Yes  → Before-save record-triggered Flow
    └── No   → Q3
decisions.rationale: All three writes land on the triggering Case; the Account and Entitlement reads are lookups, not DML. Q1's record-change branch routes to Q2 and Q2's 'Yes' leaf is the answer.
alternatives_rejected: three separate flows, one per field
decisions.consequences: No Apex means no coverage gate and no deploy-time test dependency, but also no custom exception handling: a Case whose Account has no entitlement must fall through to a documented default rather than throw (Q48).

decisions.decision: The stamping flow is before-save, not after-save: the Account and Entitlement lookups are read-only Get Records, which a before-save flow supports.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q3. Do you need any DML, an Action/callout, or an email — anything beyond
    writing fields on the triggering record?
    ├── No   → Before-Save record-triggered flow. Its element set is
                Assignment, Decision, Get Records, Loop — so a read-only
                cross-object lookup is fine here; a write is not.
decisions.rationale: Q1 'record INSERT or UPDATE' → Q2 'only set fields on the SAME record' → Q3 'no DML, no action, no email' → before-save. The branch text settles the one thing that looked like an obstacle: the cross-object read is allowed.
decisions.consequences: The customer acknowledgement (an email) cannot live in this flow; it stays in the auto-response rule (M3-S04), which is what Q63 asked for anyway.

decisions.decision: Case ownership at creation is set by Case Assignment Rules, and the assignment rule is the sole authoritative OwnerId writer at create time.
decisions.rationale: No decision tree covers this choice. automation-selection.md was checked: Q1's record-change branch leads to Q2, whose 'Yes' leaf is a before-save Flow, and the tree carries no leaf for the Lead/Case assignment-rule engine — only a Related-skills pointer that says 'Lead/Case ownership on create is a rule engine, not a Flow'. flow-pattern-selector.md was checked and has no rule-engine branch at Q1. The choice is resolved by skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md row 1 ('Route a new Lead or Case to a user or queue from field values → Assignment rule'), which is a skill reference, not a tree. Recording it as ADR-worthy rather than pretending a branch produced it.
alternatives_rejected: Omni-Channel alone with no queue-landing rule
decisions.consequences: Two by-design post-save OwnerId writers remain (Omni-Channel push in M3-S05 and the escalation rule in M4-S04). Q27 already flagged this; owner-writer-map.md in M3-S04 is the artefact that has to reconcile all three.

decisions.decision: Tier 1 receives pushed work through queue-based Omni-Channel granted by profile; Tier 2 and Billing pull from queue list views.
decisions.rationale: No decision tree covers work distribution. automation-selection.md and flow-pattern-selector.md were both read top to bottom; neither has a branch for presence-and-capacity routing. Resolved by skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md row 3 ('Distribute work from a queue to whichever agent is available and has capacity → Omni-Channel ... on top of an assignment rule that lands the record in the queue'), plus Q31, Q36 and Q37. ADR-worthy: four of the questions that shape the routing configuration (Q32-Q35) were deferred, so the configuration is provisional.
alternatives_rejected: Skills-based routing (Q37: no skill dimension in the requirement)
Per-user presence assignment (Q36: Tier 1 membership changes monthly)
decisions.consequences: Omni-Channel writes OwnerId after save, which is the second of the three owner writers D3 has to reconcile. The capacity model stays provisional until Q32-Q35 are answered.

decisions.decision: Case org-wide default stays Private and Tier 2 reaches Support cases through a criteria-based sharing rule on record type; nothing extends Billing cases to Tier 1.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q3. Can the access be described by "anyone who matches criteria X should see records matching criteria Y"?
    ├── Yes, criteria are on the record itself          → Criteria-Based Sharing Rule
decisions.rationale: Q1 'Private → Q2'; the three teams are peers, not a hierarchy, so Q2's 'No' branch leads to Q3; the access is exactly 'the Tier 2 group should see cases whose RecordType is Support', and RecordTypeId is on the record itself.
decisions.consequences: Deferred Q13 asked whether the Billing restriction is record-level or field-level. The plan takes the record-level (more restrictive) reading as assumption A1. If the answer turns out to be field-level masking, M2-S05 is re-planned, not patched.

decisions.decision: The website form posts to native Web-to-Case; no middleware, no Bulk API and no custom REST endpoint is introduced.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q5. How much volume?
    ├── < 1k rows/day                           → REST API (POST /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects)
    ├── 1k–1M rows/day                          → REST Composite (collections endpoint, up to 200/request)
    └── > 1M rows/day OR bulk upsert/delete     → Bulk API 2.0 (async ingest)
decisions.rationale: Direction 2 (external writes into Salesforce) Q5 places 60 web submissions plus 400 emails per day in the lowest band, so Bulk API 2.0 and an iPaaS are both ruled out by volume. The tree's leaf for that band names the REST API and has no leaf for native Web-to-Case or Email-to-Case at all — so the tree settles the negative half of this decision and not the positive half, which is why it is flagged ADR-worthy.
decisions.consequences: Q66 left open whether the form posts directly or through middleware. If middleware turns out to sit in front, the Origin stamping in M3-S03 and the assignment criteria in M3-S04 both change. Assumption A26 is not recorded because Q66 is answered — the answer itself says 'confirm', so the confirmation is a manual test on M3-S03.

decisions.decision: The 8-business-hour Tier 2 handoff is a Case Escalation Rule, not a scheduled Flow or a time-based Apex job.
decisions.rationale: No decision tree covers Service Cloud's escalation engine. automation-selection.md Q10 ('Scheduled job. Does it process > 50k records or run > 5 minutes?') was checked and routes between Batch Apex, chained Queueable and Schedule-triggered Flow — all three of which would re-implement an engine the platform already runs on business-hours arithmetic. async-selection.md was checked and is entered only once work has been decided to move off the transaction. Resolved by skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md ('Re-route or notify when a Case is unresolved past a time threshold → Escalation rule (Case only)') plus skills/admin/escalation-rules.
alternatives_rejected: After-save Flow with a scheduled path
decisions.consequences: The escalation engine batches, so the 480-minute threshold is not a to-the-second promise (Q46 asked for headroom to be agreed). The rule also writes OwnerId, which is the third owner writer D3 has to reconcile.

decisions.decision: Nothing in this build runs asynchronously: no @future, no Queueable, no Batch, no Schedulable and no Platform Event.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q1. How many records / how long?
    ├── < 2,000 records, < 60s          → Q2
    ├── 2k – 50k, < 5 min                → Q5 (Queueable)
    ├── > 50k OR > 5 min                 → Q8 (Batch Apex)
    └── Truly massive, one-off ETL       → Bulk API 2.0 (async SOQL / external job)
decisions.rationale: The worst case anyone described is the daily email peak of ~400 cases (Q15), and those arrive as individual API inserts, never as one 2,000-record transaction. Q1's first band applies and the tree never reaches an async tier.
decisions.consequences: Every automation in the plan runs inside the creating transaction, so the before-save flow in M4-S03 is on the critical path of every intake. If volume grows past the Q1 first band, this decision is the one to revisit.

decisions.decision: Case is treated as an ordinary object: no skinny table, no custom index request and no archival design in this phase.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q10. What stage of LDV are you in?
    ├── Designing a new high-volume object           → architect/large-data-volume-architecture (skinny + indexes from day one)
decisions.rationale: The tree was entered because the requirement names a volume (Q15: ~480 cases/day). Q1's symptom router has no branch for a greenfield design with no reported symptom, so Q10's design-stage branch is the only reachable entry. ~480/day is roughly 175k Cases a year, well below the thresholds that branch exists for, so the answer is 'not this'.
alternatives_rejected: Skinny table on Case from day one
Big Object archival of closed cases
decisions.consequences: The escalation monitoring report (M5-S01) and the queue list views (M5-S01) are unindexed selective queries today. Q76 already asked which acceptance criteria depend on volume; if the report degrades, this decision is where the revisit starts.

milestones.title: Case data model and record-type layouts
milestones.goal: Given a greenfield org with no existing Case records (Q4), when the Case model is deployed, then two record types with their Support Processes, the three active Origin values and one layout per record type exist, and every field the routing and SLA milestones reference resolves.

acceptance_tests.description: Record types, business processes and layouts agree across both steps.
Every record type, business process, field and layout produced in M1 appears in the milestone package.xml with a file behind it.

Given the Q1 answer allowed collapsing to a single record type, when the record-type decision note is read, then it states which of the two shapes was chosen and shows the Status/Reason difference that justified it.

milestones.title: Access, work pools and Case visibility
milestones.goal: Given the 18 internal users split 12 Tier 1 / 4 Tier 2 / 2 Billing (Q8), when the access model is deployed, then each team holds a permission set group over a minimal base profile, the three Case queues exist with role-and-group membership, and a Tier 1 agent cannot open a Billing case.

acceptance_tests.description: Across all five access steps: no dangerous system permission, no migratable permission left on a profile.
Across the milestone: no sharing rule contradicts the Case Private OWD.
Every permission set, PSG, profile, queue, group and sharing rule in M2 appears in the milestone package.xml with a file behind it.

The support manager and the admin lead jointly confirm that no named user is hard-coded in any queue or group and that the Billing visibility reading taken from deferred Q13 (assumption A1) is the one they want.

milestones.title: Validation, intake and routing
milestones.goal: Given a case arriving on any of the three channels (Q15), when it is created, then it has an owner from the assignment rule, the customer has an acknowledgement carrying the case number sent from support@, and no validation rule blocked the API-created record.

acceptance_tests.description: Assignment, auto-response, escalation placeholders and Email-to-Case routing hang together across the milestone.
Every Case validation rule carries the intake bypass the integration permission set grants.
Every settings file, rule set, template and Omni-Channel component in M3 appears in the milestone package.xml with a file behind it.

Given the four deferred Omni-Channel answers (Q32-Q35), when the milestone is accepted, then the support manager has signed off the provisional capacity and routing values or the Omni-Channel step is explicitly deferred to a later build.

milestones.title: SLA clocks, entitlements and escalation
milestones.goal: Given a Premier case created at 17:00 London time on a Friday (Q39), when the first-response clock is read, then it is running on the EMEA calendar, shows 4 business hours remaining, does not tick over the weekend, and the 8-business-hour Tier 2 escalation is present but inactive (Q47).

acceptance_tests.description: Across the milestone: exactly one default calendar, and every SLA component names its calendar explicitly.
Entitlement process, milestone types and the stamping flow reference the same calendars and the same entitlement.
Escalation entries name real queues and templates produced earlier in the plan.
Every BusinessHours, EntitlementProcess, MilestoneType, Flow and EscalationRules component in M4 appears in the milestone package.xml with a file behind it.

Given Q27 flagged two by-design post-save OwnerId writers (Omni-Channel and the escalation rule), when owner-writer-map.md is read alongside the escalation runbook, then both handoffs are described and neither contradicts the assignment rule.

milestones.title: Agent surfaces, sandbox proof and the deploy package
